meta.title: Model Quota
meta.description: Shows the remaining balance or the Coding Plan 5-hour / weekly quota for the active model provider below the input box.

messages.title: Model Quota
messages.historyWheelHint: Scroll up for a shorter range, down for a longer range
messages.missingCloudflareCredential: Cloudflare API token or account ID not configured
messages.settingsHint: Configure the query interval, quota history, and custom providers. Changes take effect immediately after saving.
messages.settingsNotFound: Model quota settings were not found. Disable and re-enable Model Quota on the Plugins page. If it is still unavailable, restart dsh.
messages.settingsReadOnly: The current configuration is read-only and cannot be changed here.
messages.settingsNoChanges: There are no changes to save.
messages.settingsConflict: Settings changed in another page. The latest values have been loaded; review them before saving again.
messages.queryIntervalSecondsHint: Repeat queries to the same provider reuse the last result within this window, and history samples on the same cadence (minimum 1 second). 0 queries every time. Leave blank to restore the default of 30 seconds.
messages.queryIntervalSecondsInvalid: Enter a number of 0 or greater.
messages.historyEnabledHint: Records quota changes on a timer and stores them on this machine for the quota detail chart. Enabled by default.
messages.historyDefaultRangeHint: Defaults to the last hour. Reopened quota details use this range.
messages.historyDefaultRangeInvalid: The default quota detail range is invalid.
messages.providersConfigHint: Advanced option, usually left empty. Keys are provider IDs (for example kimi-coding) and values are the override fields for that provider. Leave blank for no overrides.
messages.providersInvalid: Provider overrides must be a JSON object written as { }, each provider entry must also be an object, and provider IDs cannot be empty.
messages.providerModulesHint: Advanced option, usually left empty. Provide npm package names or absolute module paths to add quota sources the plugin does not ship with.
messages.providerModulesInvalid: Provider modules must be a valid JSON array where every item is a non-empty module name.
messages.credentialsHint: Some providers also need a console credential besides the inference API key to read quota. Credentials are stored on this machine and are never shown on the page.
messages.credentialsEffective: Takes effect on the next quota refresh (up to 1 minute).
messages.mimoCookieHint: Used by the xiaomi and xiaomi-token-plan providers. Sign in to platform.xiaomimimo.com, copy the full Cookie header from any /api/v1/ request, and keep at least serviceToken and userId.
messages.qwenTokenHint: Used by qwen-token-plan providers. Run bl auth login --console and copy access_token from ~/.bailian/config.json.
messages.xaiKeyHint: Used for the xai provider balance query. Inference API keys cannot read billing; create a read-only, team-scoped key under console.x.ai → Settings → Management Keys.
messages.adminKeyHint: Used for the anthropic and openai month-to-date usage. Plain inference keys cannot read usage: create sk-ant-admin… under Console → Settings → Admin Keys (Anthropic) or sk-admin… under platform.openai.com → Admin keys (OpenAI, organization owner only).
messages.githubTokenHint: Used for the github-copilot premium request quota. Any GitHub token works (ghp_ / gho_ / fine-grained with Plan: read).
messages.codexTokenHint: Used for the openai-codex 5-hour / weekly quota queries. Provide a ChatGPT OAuth access token (for example from the Codex CLI login); the API is private and may change.
messages.codexAccountHint: The ChatGPT-Account-Id header value used together with the token above.
messages.cloudflareTokenHint: Used for the cloudflare balance / spend query. Needs an account-level API token (AI Gateway Read / Billing Read); keep it separate from the inference token.
messages.cloudflareAccountHint: The account ID the cloudflare query targets; shown in the Cloudflare Dashboard sidebar.
messages.credentialReadOnly: This credential comes from the dsh configuration file; change it there.
messages.credentialSaved: Saved. It takes effect on the next quota refresh.
